meta.title: Reliability: exponential and Weibull failure models, MTBF
meta.tools: Constant-hazard and Weibull lifetime models, series/parallel system reliability, maximum-likelihood Weibull fitting of simulated failure data, Monte-Carlo MTBF
meta.summary: Model component lifetimes, derive the MTBF of series and redundant systems, fit Weibull parameters to test data by maximum likelihood (including censored units), and check every formula by simulating thousands of systems.
meta.problem: A board has 50 parts, each with a million-hour MTBF. How long will the board last — and does redundancy help as much as it seems?
meta.theory:
Exponential: R(t) = e^{−λt}, MTBF = 1/λ. Series of n parts: λ_sys = Σλ ⇒ 50 parts at 10⁶ h → 20,000 h. Two identical units in active parallel: MTBF = 3/(2λ) (only 1.5×, not 2×). Weibull: $R(t)=e^{-(t/η)^β}$,
mean ηΓ(1+1/β); β < 1 infant mortality, β = 1 random, β > 1 wear-out. With right-censored data, the MLE maximises Σ_failures log f + Σ_censored log R.
meta.method:
Monte Carlo: 100,000 simulated systems per configuration. Weibull test: 200 units with β = 2.5, η = 5000 h, test stopped at 4000 h (censoring ~44 % of units); MLE by optimising the censored
log-likelihood; 200 repeated experiments for parameter spread.
meta.track: Applied Mathematics — 218 projects in electrical engineering
